subject: Lumen Health MAP: evaluation milestones & GPU pool sizing (draft)
messages:
From: Tom Keller <tkeller@lumenhealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@lumenhealth.com>, procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MAP request - capacity and lead times

Rafael — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Lumen’s engineering and procurement teams want a short mutual action plan that lays out: the evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria, and an expected timeline to reserve Dedicated/private capacity (we need GPU lead times for our procurement calendar).

Key asks from our side:
- Recommended GPU pool sizing for initial pilot (expected 50k monthly inference seconds; peak concurrency ~40 requests/s)
- Typical procurement lead time for Dedicated (order -> RDY) and Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Steps and ownership to move from eval -> signed reservation (MAY/JUN quarter cadence)

Could you send over a draft MAP with milestones we can share internally? Procurement also asked for any SOC2 evidence while contracts are discussed.

Thanks,
Tom
VP, Digital Platforms
Lumen Health
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Tom Keller <tkeller@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP request - capacity and lead times

Tom — great to connect. I put a compact MAP draft together below and attached a workbook that maps milestones to owner and deliverables (see Lumen_MAP_v1.xlsx). High-level summary here:

1) Pilot eval (2–4 weeks)
   - Goals: validate latency SLOs at 90th pct, token-cost targets, and correctness on 4 canonical prompts
   - Owners: Lumen Eng (tests), Redwood SE (setup + runbook)
   - Deliverable: Eval report + perf baseline

2) Scale validation (4 weeks)
   - Goals: throughput stress tests to target concurrency, batch profile, KV/prefix cache exercise
   - Owners: Lumen Eng, Redwood Infra (load harness)
   - Deliverable: Sizing recommendation (GPU tranches)

3) Procurement & reservation window (6–12 weeks depending on tranche)
   - Dedicated: typical lead time 6–10 weeks for reserved pools (region-dependent)
   - Private (VPC): 8–12 weeks for setup + network approvals; on-prem varies (12+ weeks)
   - Owners: Redwood Sales (contract & capacity), Lumen Procurement

4) Onboarding & acceptance (2–4 weeks)
   - Final acceptance tests and runbook handoff.

Notes and contingencies:
- For an initial pilot sized for ~40 req/s peak and 50k inference seconds/month we recommend a small tranche: equivalent to 4 x A100-class GPUs (quantized execution) with autoscaling headroom for spikes.
- If Lumen wants aggressive lead times, we can supply a temporary burst pool from Hosted inventory while Dedicated procures — this reduces service disruption risk.

I copied Marissa and Karthik for commercial cadence and Neha for SRE/SE sizing. I’ll loop back after engineering confirms the perf targets you’ll run. Also attaching our SOC2 attestation for procurement.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Team — forwarding Tom’s asks (below). Need quick confirmation on two items so I can update the MAP and return to them next week:
1) For 40 req/s peak + 50k inference-sec/mo what is your conservative GPU tranche recommendation (A100 equiv, 16/32GB variants, quantized)?
2) Can we commit to temporary burst access from Hosted while Dedicated pool is provisioned? Any cost guidance?

Tom expects procurement timelines on the order of 6–12 weeks; they want explicit milestones for contract -> capacity provisioning. I’d like a concise paragraph for the MAP that we can give procurement outlining lead times and owners.

Thanks — Rafael
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Lumen MAP — quick sizing ask + procurement timeline

Rafael / team — quick sizing thoughts from infra:
- Baseline recommendation: 4 x A100-40GB equiv (quantized runtime) for the pilot; allows ~45–60 req/s depending on prompt length and batching.
- If Lumen uses long context windows (>2k tokens) plan for +1 GPU for KV cache pressure.
- Dedicated lead time: 6–10 weeks (US-west region) assuming no custom network appliances.
- Private VPC onboarding: 8–12 weeks (includes customer VPC peering and certs).
- Hosted burst: yes, we can offer a 4-week burst pool sized to match pilot at the hosted rate + short-term premium (T&Cs in attached workbook).

I added notes into the workbook and a short paragraph you can paste into the MAP.

-Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood

1) Can you confirm invoicing cadence for Dedicated reservations (monthly/quarterly) and whether credits apply if we underutilize a tranche?
2) For the hosted burst option, please indicate any minimum commitment and the expected uplift in unit pricing.
3) We also need your SOC2 summary page with scope (does it include hosting for dedicated/private?) — thanks for the attestation but procurement needs the scope table.

If you can provide answers + an updated MAP worksheet with owner columns (we saw an early draft) by 2 June, procurement will fast-track review.

Regards,
Lumen Procurement Team
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Cc: Tom Keller <tkeller@lumenhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP request - capacity and lead times — procurement questions

Team — appreciate the clarity. Short answers below and attached updated MAP workbook (Lumen_MAP_v1.xlsx) with owner columns and timing.

1) Invoicing cadence: Dedicated reservations are invoiced monthly in arrears against committed units. Underutilization credits: we offer a usage true-up model — if utilization is <50% in a billing month, a partial credit applies (details in contract appendix).
2) Hosted burst: minimum 2-week window; pricing uplift ~25% over standard hosted unit rates. No long-term commitment required for the burst.
3) SOC2 scope: attached SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf includes scope table; it covers Redwood hosted services and dedicated control plane. For Private/on‑prem, scope is limited to the control plane and management interfaces — we’ve noted that in the workbook and will provide an addendum for fully air-gapped installs.

Next steps:
- We’ll schedule a 30-minute procurement sync (suggest Thu 6/4 or Fri 6/5).
- Once procurement confirms the preferred tranche and invoicing model we’ll issue a mutual action plan with explicit dates for PO, provisioning kickoff, and acceptance gates.

Thanks — Rafael
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
